metadata.note: The Tennessee and North Carolina Railroad (Railway from the June 1920 reorganization - same operator, same superintendent, not a Rule 4 split): a ~21-mile logging road from Newport, Tenn., up the Pigeon River and Big Creek to Champion Lumber's Crestmont mill in Haywood County, N.C., and lessee 1912/13-1928 of the separate Pigeon River Railway, West Canton - Sunburst ('Pigeon River Division'), never physically connected to it. Drawn only at the passenger years the research confirms (research/branches/tennessee_and_north_carolina_railroad.txt). The T&NC's third passenger operation, the leased Smoky Mountain Railroad Knoxville - Sevierville ('Knoxville Branch', 1927-1938), is drawn in smoky_mountain_railroad.geojson in the same company colour, which this file's colour was copied from programmatically.
sources: The Newport Plain Talk (Newport, Tenn.), Chronicling America sn89058216, issues 1911-1918 (per-segment URLs)
geometry_sources: Approximation, not a trace: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) waterway centrelines via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), shortest path along the river between Nominatim/OSM place nodes (each geocode checked for type; bad ones hand-pinned), Douglas-Peucker 8 m then opstrace.trim_reversals. opstrace.py found no T&NC track to trace (see geometry_quality).
metadata.freight_only_audit: Nothing freight-only drawn (Rule 1): the Newport line's 1919-1937 years (unproven either way; the line closed 1 Jan 1938), the Champion/Suncrest logging lines up Big Creek above Crestmont and the Laurel Fork Junction lumber siding, the never-completed Waterville - Canton extension through the Pigeon gorge (construction/logging), Champion's lines above Sunburst, the Pigeon River Railway's own 1928-1932 operation (Lake Logan dam traffic), and the Andrews - Hayesville 'Peavine' (no passenger evidence) are all omitted. The post-1926 Canton - Sunburst 'daily bus service' was a road bus.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN END, Newport - Crestmont: passenger service confirmed to 1918 only. When it actually ended (anywhere 1919-1937; the line closed 1 Jan 1938) is unsourced. NPS dates the railroad 1902-1918, which conflicts with the 1921-22 NC Corporation Commission report and taplines.net (Newport - Crestmont still operated in the 1920s). Would settle it: Official Guide 1919-1937 T&NC entries, the ICC valuation report, branchline.uk Fowler letters, the Waynesville Mountaineer.

OPEN START, Newport - Crestmont: 1911 is the first year of the searchable newspaper run; completion is given as 1901 (NPT 1915-02-24), 1902 (NPS) or 'operational 1908' / Crestmont reached Sept 1909 (carolana.com). Whether Mount Sterling was the terminal before Crestmont (an extension, or a rename) is unresolved.
Whether service was ever cut back from Crestmont to Waterville after logging ended in 1919 (NPS describes a 'spur line up Big Creek').

Newport terminal: weekday trains were timed from 'Newport', Sunday ones from 'Newport Junction' (one mile out). Whether passenger trains used the Southern depot or stopped at Newport Junction is not established; the drawing runs to the Southern depot.

ANCHOR/OPEN, Pigeon River Division: only 1913 is confirmed. The end of passenger service (anywhere 1913-1928 under the T&NC, or to 1932) is unsourced; whether the passenger train reached Sunburst in 1913 or stopped short at the Penland place; whether the Nov 1913 Sunburst - Spruce extension opened; the date of the undated carolana.com schedule.
Pigeon River Division mileage conflict: 16.00 mi (1913 report) vs 13 mi (NPT 1913-02-13) vs 'twelve miles' (SMN) vs 14.95 mi West Canton - Spruce (1921-22 report).
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates (see segment notes and speed_source).

The UTK Prince collection folder 'Tennessee & North Carolina Railroad: Rail Passenger Bus, 1927-1936' - Newport line or Knoxville Branch? Title only; if the former it would be the only late-era passenger evidence on Newport - Crestmont.

properties.line: Tennessee and North Carolina: Newport – Crestmont
properties.speed_source: estimate, unsourced: no running time is recoverable from the 1911 timetable (only departure times from each end were printed); 12-15 mph assumed for a mountain logging road (research/branches/tennessee_and_north_carolina_railroad.txt, UNRESOLVED)
properties.geometry_source: Approximation, not a trace: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) waterway centrelines via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), shortest path along the river between Nominatim/OSM place nodes (each geocode checked for type; bad ones hand-pinned), Douglas-Peucker 8 m then opstrace.trim_reversals. opstrace.py found no T&NC track to trace (see geometry_quality).
properties.geometry_quality: No T&NC track survives in OpenStreetMap: no way in the region carries old_railway_operator for any spelling probed ('T&NC', 'Tennessee and North Carolina', 'Tennessee & North Carolina', 'Pigeon River Railway' - the only old_railway_operator value present is 'Southern'); no railway=abandoned/razed or historic=railway way lies on either corridor; OpenHistoricalMap returned no railway ways in either corridor; and the Big Creek Trail (the old logging grade) begins at the Big Creek picnic area and runs UP Big Creek, i.e. it is the excluded Champion logging line above Crestmont, not the passenger line below it. An opstrace.trace run over the available rail/trail graph snapped the waypoints 0.4-2.9 km off onto unrelated Southern/industrial track and returned mostly chords, so it was discarded. APPROXIMATED, whole line (22.03 mi): drawn along the OSM centreline of the Pigeon River (Newport - Hartford - Waterville, 19.96 mi) and Big Creek (Waterville - Mount Sterling - Crestmont, 1.96 mi), as a proxy for the lifted grade, which ran beside these streams through the gorge. Legs: Newport (Southern depot) - Edwina 5.07 mi; Edwina - Hartford 10.41 mi; Hartford - Waterville 4.81 mi; Waterville - Mount Sterling 0.75 mi; Mount Sterling - Crestmont 0.88 mi; plus straight connectors from the river to the end points (120 m at Newport, 169 m at Crestmont). The river line sits in the stream bed, typically tens to a few hundred metres from where the track actually ran, and follows every meander the railroad may have cut across. Straight chords between the same points would total 16.1 mi. Drawn 22.03 mi against 21 mi documented Newport - Crestmont (Knoxville Sentinel via Newport Plain Talk 1911-06-22; 1908 NC Corporation Commission report, Newport - Mt. Sterling 21 mi) - about 5% long. End points: Newport is drawn from the OSM 'Newport Depot' (the Southern station); the T&NC's own terminal was Newport Junction 'one mile distance from Newport', not located, and whether weekday trains ran into the Southern depot is not established - the last mile at Newport is uncertain. Crestmont is pinned at the foot of the Big Creek Trail by the Big Creek picnic area/ranger station, the generally given site of the vanished mill town; no depot site is located (Nominatim's 'Crestmont' was a street near Waynesville and its 'Mount Sterling' a peak - both rejected; Mount Sterling uses the OSM hamlet node). Wilton, Edwina and Newport Junction depot sites are not located; Edwina is a place node 118 m from the line, Hartford 279 m. LATER ALIGNMENT: the river centreline is today's, after I-40 (built through the Pigeon gorge 1960s) and the Walters hydro plant at Waterville (c.1927-30) reshaped the banks; the 1911-18 track position is not established anywhere along the line.

segments.note: Regular scheduled passenger service, Newport - Hartford - Waterville - Mount Sterling - Crestmont, steam, with separate passenger and freight crews. 1911 is the first year of the SEARCHABLE record (the Newport Plain Talk on loc.gov begins March 1911), not the start of service: the road was completed c.1901 and reached Crestmont c.1909, so service very likely ran earlier, but no earlier passenger year is confirmed - do not extend backward without evidence. One train a day each way until May 1911; from May 1911 two round trips daily except Sunday (lv Newport 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., lv Crestmont 6 a.m. and 2 p.m., connecting with Southern Nos. 101 and 11), a Sunday round trip (lv Newport Junction 9 a.m., lv Crestmont 4 p.m.) begun as a summer Sunday excursion train, and a Saturday-night week-ender; 20-page illustrated timetable booklet, June 1911. Church excursion Sept 1912; 'Pennsylvania railroad cars' put in service Newport - Crestmont early 1913; trestle near Hartford washed out Mar 1913, 'passengers were transferred'; 'the regular passenger train' May 1913. headway_min 480 is an ESTIMATE derived from the 1911 schedule (two departures each way, eight hours apart, ex Sunday); it is not a published headway.
sources: Segment-level: dates and service pattern from the Newport Plain Talk issues listed (Chronicling America); headway_min is an estimate derived from the 1911 schedule.

segments.note: Passenger trains confirmed only by public fare-paying specials: county-fair daily specials Crestmont - Newport Junction and return, Oct 1914 (advertisement signed W. J. Parks, superintendent); a special for soldiers and their families, Crestmont - Newport, 'making the usual stops', June 1918. No regular timetable for 1914-1918 has been checked: headway_min 480 is carried forward from the 1911 schedule as an ESTIMATE and is NOT SOURCED for these years. 1918 is the last CONFIRMED passenger year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. The road ran (freight at least) until it closed 1 Jan 1938 (abandonment, not a passenger end); logging at Crestmont ended 1919; NPS dates the railroad '1902-1918', conflicting with the 1921-22 NC report and taplines.net, which still show Newport - Crestmont operated in the 1920s. Do not extend without evidence. Receivership from 13 Sep 1916 - same company and operator.
sources: Segment-level: 1914 and 1918 specials from the Newport Plain Talk issues listed. NOT SOURCED for the headway, which is carried forward from 1911 as an estimate, or for any regular schedule in these years.

properties.line: Tennessee and North Carolina: Pigeon River Division
properties.speed_source: estimate from an UNDATED schedule (carolana.com, T&NC #3): 75 min each way West Canton - Sunburst, i.e. 10-13 mph over the conflicting 13-16 mi figures; not tied to 1913
properties.geometry_source: Approximation, not a trace: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) waterway centrelines via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), shortest path along the river between Nominatim/OSM place nodes (each geocode checked for type; bad ones hand-pinned), Douglas-Peucker 8 m then opstrace.trim_reversals. opstrace.py found no T&NC track to trace (see geometry_quality).
properties.geometry_quality: No T&NC track survives in OpenStreetMap: no way in the region carries old_railway_operator for any spelling probed ('T&NC', 'Tennessee and North Carolina', 'Tennessee & North Carolina', 'Pigeon River Railway' - the only old_railway_operator value present is 'Southern'); no railway=abandoned/razed or historic=railway way lies on either corridor; OpenHistoricalMap returned no railway ways in either corridor; and nothing of the Pigeon River Railway survives along NC 110 / Lake Logan Road. An opstrace.trace run over the available rail/trail graph snapped the waypoints 0.4-2.9 km off onto unrelated Southern/industrial track and returned mostly chords, so it was discarded. APPROXIMATED, whole line (15.30 mi): drawn along the OSM waterway=river centreline of the Pigeon River (upstream from West Canton through Canton past the Champion mill, to Bethel) and its West Fork (Bethel - Sunburst), as a proxy for the lifted grade, which followed the river. Legs: West Canton - Bethel 8.08 mi (Bethel place node is 684 m off the river line); Bethel - Sunburst 6.82 mi; plus straight connectors of 1180 m due east from the West Canton hamlet node to the river (joining it upstream of the meander north of Canton, which the line would not have looped round) and 139 m from the river to the Sunburst node. LAKE-FLOODED: the last 0.84 mi into Sunburst lies inside the Lake Logan reservoir (impounded 1932); there it follows OSM's river line through the lake, which is a drawing convention, not a surveyed former channel, and the Sunburst node is the GNIS placement of a village now under the water, not a depot site. Drawn 15.30 mi against the documented figures, which conflict: 16.00 mi West Canton - Sunburst (15th NC Corporation Commission report, 1913, via carolana.com), 13 mi (Newport Plain Talk 1913-02-13), 'a short twelve miles' (Smoky Mountain News); 14.95 mi West Canton - Spruce (1921-22 report) is inconsistent with all of them, since Spruce lay four miles beyond Sunburst. The drawing is close to the 1913 report's 16.00 mi. Where the West Canton connection with the Southern actually was is not established. Ends at Sunburst: the Sunburst - Spruce extension (announced for 1 Nov 1913) is not drawn. LATER ALIGNMENT: today's river line, through a reservoir that did not exist in 1913.

segments.note: ANCHOR and OPEN: 1913 is the only CONFIRMED passenger year on the Pigeon River Division, the Champion-tied Pigeon River Railway (West Canton - Bethel - Sunburst) leased to and operated by the Tennessee and North Carolina from late 1912. Regular passenger service was announced for 'by March 1st' 1913 (Newport Plain Talk 1913-02-13), and on 25 Jul 1913 'A regular passenger schedule is operated and a large volume of traffic handled' (Jackson County Journal). Service certainly ran wider than this one year in both directions, but no other year is confirmed: the T&NC lease ran to 1928 and the line closed 1932 (abandonment dates, not passenger ends). Do not widen without evidence. Early in 1913 passengers for the upper end may have ridden freight trains from the Penland place. Drawn to Sunburst only: freight and passenger trains were announced to run on to Spruce, four miles above Sunburst, from 1 Nov 1913 (Newport Plain Talk 1913-10-23), but that is unconfirmed. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE from an undated schedule (lv Sunburst 7:15 a.m., lv West Canton 10:35 a.m., daily except Sunday - one round trip) that is not tied to any year.
sources: Segment-level: 1913 service from the Jackson County Journal 1913-07-25 and the Newport Plain Talk issues listed; headway_min is an estimate from an undated schedule not checked against 1913.
